findings.rule: density-tiers (deep dive: ONE focal element that wins on weight)
findings.evidence: The two-column grid puts a 7-row pressures deck (ends ~y830) next to a 34-row segment table (ends ~y2460). That leaves about 1,600px of empty left column. The anatomy diagram is the natural focal element and the table's visual output, yet it starts around y2780. It is centred in a ~480px box with empty space on both sides and is never on screen together with the table that colours it. The segment table also runs past its deck's right edge, cutting off the plaque/occlusion columns.
findings.recommendation: This is a relocation, not a restyle, so it routes to redesign. Move the anatomy diagram (with its legend and drawing toolbar) into the left column directly under the pressures deck. Make it sticky (stays in view on scroll, top offset below the header) so it stays beside the segment table while scrolling. Give the table the full right-column width so all columns fit inside the deck.

findings.rule: density-tiers (boldness is spent once per screen) + Buttons
findings.evidence: About 8 solid gradient buttons compete: the back button, + add study, templates, three equal-weight footer buttons (save draft, PDF preview, PDF download) and + add recommendation. These buttons are the heaviest things on screen, heavier than any clinical content. Section headers also stack a tick bar with an icon tile, and each title has the same weight and size as its subtitle.
findings.recommendation: Keep exactly one --emr-gradient-primary button: footer 'PDF ჩამოტვირთვა'. Make save-draft, PDF preview, templates, + add study and + add recommendation secondary buttons (white deck + hairline border). Make the back button a ghost button. In section headers, drop the icon tiles and keep the 4×15 gradient tick bar alone. Set the title to --emr-font-md/600 and step the subtitle down to secondary text.

findings.evidence: In bilateral mode every Georgian segment name is printed twice in a row at full weight, once for the R row and once for the L row. That is 17 names × 2 across 34 rows. At 1440 the script did not flag it. My judgment: this repeats row labels, not data values (the R and L rows hold different data), so it is layout bloat rather than progressive disclosure. It doubles the label ink and makes the table twice as tall to scan.
findings.recommendation: Print each segment name once, as a group label spanning its two sub-rows. The R and L sub-rows then carry only the side chip and their inputs.

findings.evidence: The autosave indicator in the footer ('ბოლოს შენახული: 15:28:38') uses a red dot. Red otherwise means hemodynamically significant stenosis (diagram, legend) and the moderate-PAD ABI chip. The dot is small and low-stakes, so this is one minor borrow.
findings.recommendation: Make the autosave dot neutral (--emr-text-secondary). Use --emr-error only if saving actually fails, and then with an explicit failure label.

reasoning: Density tier was supplied as deep-dive; I used the matching light reference, deep-dive.png. The eye first goes to the scattered solid-navy buttons, then to the ABI chips. Severity colour itself is well disciplined: red appears only on the SFA-prox 70–99% segment, its legend and the moderate-PAD ABI chip, and grey/black are kept for normal/occlusion. The structure is what fails. Page and cards are both pure white, so nothing groups. A short pressures card next to a 34-row table leaves a dead column, and the diagram that should be the focal element sits far below the fold. No rule covers two other problems, so they are not scored: the segment table is clipped at its right edge, and the pressures table lists L before R while the side toggle, segment rows, distal runoff and diagram all list R first. That left/right inconsistency is a clinical-safety concern to escalate as a product decision. The agent definition cites 'Content & layout' rules 1–9, but DESIGN-DIRECTION.md has no such section, so no findings rest on them. Biggest fix: move the anatomy diagram into the left column as a sticky panel beside the segment table.

findings.evidence: The anatomy silhouette keeps its light fill in dark mode, so it becomes the brightest slab on the page. Its R/L side labels are effectively invisible (light text on the light silhouette). The legend's black 'ოკლუზია' (occlusion) swatch and the black drawing-toolbar swatch nearly vanish against the dark card. In dark mode a clinician cannot read the most severe grade from the legend, or the laterality from the diagram.

reasoning: Density tier was supplied as deep-dive. The screenshot and metrics both say dark, and I judged against the matching dark reference, deep-dive-dark.png. Unlike light mode, the decks do separate from the page (bg-card vs bg-page contrast 1.22, with shadow), so depth ordering exists and hierarchy reaches 2. The diagram also wins on brightness, but only far below the fold, and it achieves that by glaring rather than by design. The same structural problems as light remain: a dead left column, the diagram far from the table that drives it, and too many filled buttons. Dark mode adds a severity-legibility problem: the occlusion swatch and the diagram's R/L labels almost disappear. The pressures table also lists L before R, inconsistent with the rest of the screen; no rule covers this, so it is unscored but should be escalated. Biggest fix: put the diagram in a sticky left-column panel beside the segment table and make its silhouette, labels and swatches follow the theme.
